subject.title: feat(session): add named new and close chat commands

question: Should OpenClaw core accept chat-level `/close`/`/delete` plus explicit `/new --name` after the parser and proof gaps are fixed, or should destructive session cleanup stay in UI/session-management surfaces for now?
rationale: The parser defect is mechanical, but adding destructive chat commands changes a user-facing session lifecycle surface and needs maintainer product ownership beyond CI.

options.title: Fix then sponsor the command surface
options.body: Require the catalog-backed parser repair and current-head proof, then continue reviewing the feature as a core chat session-management command set.

options.title: Narrow to naming only
options.body: Ask the contributor to keep explicit `/new --name` and defer `/close`/`/delete` until a separate session cleanup decision lands.

options.title: Supersede with UI/title work
options.body: Close or pause this PR if maintainers want https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93587 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95182 to own the near-term naming direction instead.

recommendation.title: Fix then sponsor the command surface
recommendation.body: Require the catalog-backed parser repair and current-head proof, then continue reviewing the feature as a core chat session-management command set.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on session lifecycle and command-adjacent session management changes in the current codebase evidence.
